title: `ARG_MIN`/`ARG_MAX`: rows with a NULL on either side are skipped
verdict: FIRST(x ORDER BY y) over the rows where neither is NULL; ties are the engine's
description: `ARG_MIN(x, y)` gives `x` at the row with the smallest `y`, over the rows where neither `x` nor `y` is NULL (`ARG_MIN_NULL` keeps a NULL `x`). No such rows give NULL. Doubles compare in DuckDB's order, NaN above `+inf`. Of rows that tie on `y` it keeps the one it met first, so ties depend on the order it reads the rows. `ARG_MAX` is the same with the largest `y`.
reference: The parser reads `arg_min(x, y)` as `FIRST(x ORDER BY y)` with the filter `y IS NOT NULL` (`AggFn.pick`, #53), and `arg_max` with `ORDER BY y DESC`; `FIRST` skips a NULL `x`. Ties are the engine's: `Rel.windowsTotal` reports the result as determined only when the group's and the order's columns contain a key.
